references.text: Caiaphas's prophecy that it is better for one man to die for the people is immediately explained as a divine revelation concerning Jesus's atoning death, which directly connects to his role as high priest in this verse.
John refers back to Caiaphas's advice from this chapter when he describes his decision to hand Jesus over to be put to death, confirming that he was the one who gave this counsel.

The Letter to the Hebrews contrasts Caiaphas's annual sacrificial role with Jesus's eternal sacrifice, where Jesus as high priest offered himself once for all, in contrast to the yearly ceremony Caiaphas represented.

The description of the high priest entering the Holy Place alone once a year corresponds with Caiaphas's title as 'high priest that year' in this verse and underscores the limitation of the old covenant system.
The counsel from the chief priests and Pharisees that Jesus must die to save the nation from the Romans is the immediate context for Caiaphas's intervention in this verse.
